source.title: Intelligent Lithology Identification Methods for Rock Images Based on Object Detection
source.authors: Zhen-Long Hou; Ji-Kang Wei; Jin-Rong Shen; Xin-Wei Liu; Wen-Tian Zhao

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study varies batch size and measures identification accuracy on a held-out image dataset, conceptually testing whether larger batches worsen held-out performance.
record.gate_note: Only V5 is tested. The study reports batch-size results for improved SSD and DGS; it does not test random-label memorization, width scaling, optimizer comparisons, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.test_reason: The study tests V5 in a new setting: rock-image lithology identification. It varies batch size from 4 to 128 at a fixed 200 epochs and learning rate of 1 × 10⁻⁴, and reports testing accuracy.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the batch-size conclusion: smaller batches generally yield higher testing accuracy despite higher final training loss, and the authors select batch size 4 with learning rate 1 × 10⁻⁴ for their methods.
record.recipe_differences: Rock-image object detection and lithology classification, with an 80/20 train-test split; batch-size sweeps use a fixed 200-epoch setting and test identification accuracy.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes held-out accuracy and training loss; the tested learning rate also changes accuracy and loss, but learning rate is outside the listed versions.
record.problems: One geographic area and dataset; the testing set is drawn from augmented rock images. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Batch-size results are reported for these two methods only.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width scaling beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparisons and tuning-dependent differences; Adam is used without an optimizer ablation.
Longer training, learning-rate scaling with warmup, normalization or regularization adaptations, and whether an adapted recipe removes the fixed-epoch penalty.
Effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay.
Measured magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

missing.what: Final training losses at batch sizes 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, and 128 are 0.016, 0.010, 0.005, 0.004, 0.003, and 0.004. Larger batches therefore have lower final training loss despite worse testing accuracy.
missing.locator: Performance Analysis, Figure 10 and accompanying text, pages 2976–2977.

record.verdict_notes: The numerical accuracy values match the supplied text. DGS and improved SSD share the trained network and are not independent replications. Images were augmented before the 80/20 split, leaving independence between training and testing source images unclear. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Sharp-minimum explanations are attributed to prior work; this study does not measure sharpness.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning or weight-decay recipes.
Language models, other image classifiers, comparisons with smaller batches under varying epoch budgets, and recipe adaptations such as longer training, warmup, or normalization changes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Improved SSD with Adam, fixed 200 epochs and learning rate 1 × 10⁻⁴, batch sizes 8–128 versus 4.
relationships.reason: R1–R6 show testing accuracy falling from 89.4% at batch size 4 to 59.0%, 38.1%, 24.5%, 22.3%, and 16.8% at larger batches.
relationships.display_finding: The study's results suggest testing accuracy declined substantially as batch size increased. These results have not been verified.

relationships.condition: DGS geographic/database postprocessing of the same improved SSD batch-size sweep.
relationships.reason: R7–R12 show testing accuracy of 98.4% at batch size 4 versus 49.0–84.2% at larger batches; constraints preserve the penalty.
relationships.display_finding: The study's results suggest geographic and database postprocessing retained the smaller-batch accuracy advantage. These results have not been verified.
